_: Curated geography: the strongest source, because a person read the article.
Everything else in geo.json is generated, so a correction made in the output
lasts until the next build and no longer. These last. Each entry says why,
and the panel labels them so a reader can tell a hand-read pin from a claim
Wikidata made. Added when a flag on the published map turns out to be right.
`place` pins a referent; `unplace` suppresses whatever the passes found.

buckskin fringe.why: no Wikipedia link; buckskins are Native American deerskin clothing, later taken up by frontiersmen

cherufe (chilean magma creature).why: Mapuche, and the Mapuche hop named Chile and Argentina; the Andes region centroid sits far north of it

epaulettes.why: its article's History section: 17th-century French military dress, and the word is French for 'little shoulder'

european dragon.why: its own article; same cluster, same gap

huma bird.why: Persian, but it sits in the firebird cluster and so inherited Slavic & Eastern Europe

iberian sculpture (bicha of balazote).why: Iberian, but 'people Iberians (Spain)' named the Iberian Peninsula and Occitania, so the hop was refused

inuksuk.why: Inuit; 'culture Inuit' named four countries, so the hop was refused

japanese dragon.why: its own article; the dragon cluster is rightly tied to no one place, so nothing else reaches it

japanese war fan.why: was reached through 'a kind of hand fan', which is no evidence; the thing is Japanese regardless

king ghidorah.why: was right only by luck, through 'a kind of movie monster'; Toho, 1964

lamassu.why: Assyrian, but it sits in the chimera cluster and so inherited Greece & Rome

mongolian laminar armour.why: no Wikipedia link, so no pass could ask; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongolian_armour

nepenthes lower pitcher.why: no Wikipedia link; the genus's native range, so an area rather than a spot

tessen (japanese war fan).why: as japanese war fan — same article, same reason

the iron wolf of lithuania.why: Lithuanian, from the founding legend of Vilnius; its cluster's culture area said Slavic & Eastern Europe, and Lithuanian is Baltic, not Slavic

tree-kangaroo.why: its article's Distribution section: New Guinea, far NE Australia and the islands between

zmei gorynych.why: Zmei (Russian folklore); same cluster, same gap

zmora.why: Polish; nesting it under the mare cluster made it inherit that cluster's Western Europe

unplace.asian black bear: its range runs from southeastern Iran through the Himalayas and mainland Southeast Asia to China, Korea, Japan and the Russian Far East — six of this map's regions, so any single pin would be a guess dressed as a fact
unplace.bearded vulture: its own entry claims it is endemic to the Sela Pass; it ranges across the mountains of Eurasia and Africa, and a single Himalayan pass is a sighting
unplace.hadrosaur: was pinned to the Kanguk Formation, one Arctic site standing in for a clade on five continents; its sibling clade-level referents carry no pin either
unplace.tailor: reached Germany one hop out through 'a kind of Q778000'; a trade is from nowhere
unplace.white stork: its own entry claims it is endemic to the Little Rann of Kutch, a salt marsh it winters in; it breeds across Europe, West Asia and NW Africa and winters in Africa and India, so no one place is where it is from
